sections.overview: The Pacific Golden Plover is a migratory shorebird that breeds in Arctic Siberia and Alaska.
sections.identification: Its upperparts are golden-spangled, with black underparts in breeding plumage. Compared with the European Golden Plover (P. apricaria), it has grey-brown rather than white axillaries, a useful distinction in flight. The Grey Plover (P. squatarola) has black axillaries.
sections.habitat: It nests on Arctic tundra and uses coasts, beaches, mudflats and other open ground across its broad non-breeding range.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on insects, molluscs, worms, crustaceans and spiders; berries also form part of its tundra-season diet.
sections.behavior: It undertakes long-distance migration, wintering from Pacific islands and Australasia to parts of Asia and the Indian Ocean region.
sections.reproduction: On the Arctic breeding grounds, adults nest on the ground and both sexes defend nesting territories.
sections.ecology: It is a close relative of the European Golden Plover (Pluvialis apricaria), whose breeding range and main wintering region are much farther west; P. fulva instead breeds in Siberia and Alaska and winters broadly across the Pacific and Indian Oceans.
sections.conservation: BirdLife lists it as Least Concern globally, while noting evidence of decline in the Australian population over several decades.
